clue.text: She may suggest a hold-up in social drinking

definitions.text: She may suggest a hold-up in social drinking

parts.words: She may suggest a hold-up in social drinking
parts.note: a woman who proposes the raising of glasses at a formal dinner; 'hold-up' sounds like a robbery but is a lifting of drinks

explanation.surface: A woman at a party seems to be planning a robbery among the drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suggest' is to propose, and the 'hold-up' is the raising of glasses at a banquet, not a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A female master of ceremonies at a banquet proposes the toasts, prompting guests to lift their glasses.

clue.text: First-class vessel commander sent over for Mark's wife

indicators.note: sending the whole string over turns it backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 as I
a vat is a large vessel
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A captain of a fine ship is dispatched to fetch a man's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent over' reverses AI + VAT + CO; Mark is Mark Antony, who married the sister of Octavian.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony's Roman wife, sister of Augustus, as in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Rebel stage — not dressed properly

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
soldiers who are not dressed are not aligned in rank, so out of line

explanation.surface: A theatrical uprising staged by actors in the wrong costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: On parade, troops 'dress' by lining up exactly, so 'not dressed properly' means misaligned, not badly clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to break with rules or behave defiantly, behaving improperly against authority.

clue.text: Calm down, given second fill-up with last of whisky

parts.note: mo is a short moment, a second

indicators.note: fill is stirred up, so its letters are rearranged
the final letter of whisky is taken

explanation.surface: A drinker is soothed by a refill topped off with the end of the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like an ordinal before 'fill-up', but it is the noun for a moment; 'up' is the anagram signal and 'last of' takes the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mollify is to soothe someone's anger, to placate or pacify them.

clue.text: Offer revolutionary afterthought about disastrous revue

indicators.note: the turned postscript goes around the jumbled show
revolving turns the postscript letters round

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

indicators.note: a disastrous show falls apart, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A critic adds a revolutionary postscript to a review of a flop of a revue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses PS to SP, which goes 'about' ERVEU, from REVUE jumbled by 'disastrous'.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve up is to present or provide something, as a dish or an idea.

clue.text: Be provoked by winding-up process, seeing cast put out?

definitions.text: Be provoked by winding-up process, seeing cast put out?

parts.words: Be provoked by winding-up process, seeing cast put out?
parts.note: teasing (winding up) provokes someone, while an angler winds the reel to bring in the lure after casting it out

explanation.surface: A company in liquidation angers the actors who lose their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding-up' suggests closing a company and 'cast' a troupe of actors, but both belong to fishing: a fish snaps at the lure cast out.
explanation.definitionFit: To react angrily to deliberate provocation, as a fish seizes a hook.

clue.text: Finances energy source that's just below the earth's surface

definitions.text: that's just below the earth's surface

parts.note: subs finances, as in lending someone money
oil is burned as a fuel

explanation.surface: A firm funds a fuel supply found close underground.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'sub' someone is to lend or advance them money.
explanation.definitionFit: The layer beneath topsoil, lying just under the ground.

clue.text: State of bliss — also of despair, when disillusioned

indicators.note: being disillusioned breaks the arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Bliss is also a kind of despair once illusions fade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when disillusioned' rearranges ALSO OF DESPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A happiness founded on illusion or ignorance of reality, a delusive contentment.

clue.text: Pot-smokers insist on skinning up -there's trouble in store

parts.note: heads is slang for cannabis users
will is to insist determinedly
skinning up is rolling a joint, so roll

explanation.surface: Cannabis users demand to roll another joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinning up' is slang for making a cannabis cigarette with rolling papers (skins).
explanation.definitionFit: A warning that people will be punished or dismissed, as by beheading.

clue.text: Have a bit of a go at me, already serving porridge?

indicators.note: having just a bit of the following words means taking a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone invites a friend to have a go at them over breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a bit of' tells you to take a run of letters from 'a go at me, already'; 'serving' just links that run to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is made by boiling rolled or ground oats in water or milk.

clue.text: Ludicrous outbreak of bile, after knight's retreated

indicators.note: the bile letters come after the knight's letters
going back means the knight's title is read from right to left

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters the word bile, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a sudden burst of bile absurd once a knight has backed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreated' is the reversal signal, 'outbreak of' the anagram signal, and 'after' fixes the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laughable or absurd is ludicrous; both describe what invites ridicule.

clue.text: Enjoy "early" retirement, having been kicked upstairs?

definitions.text: Enjoy "early" retirement, having been kicked upstairs?

parts.words: Enjoy "early" retirement, having been kicked upstairs?
parts.note: 'early' hides 'earl-y', like a peer, and being kicked upstairs is a politician's elevation to the House of ...

explanation.surface: Someone happily takes early retirement after being promoted out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'kicked upstairs' is promotion to remove someone from power, as when a British MP is sent to the House of Lords; the quoted 'early' winks at an earl.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to live in great luxury, as a wealthy aristocrat would.

clue.text: See 12
See 12
See 3

Pestilential pupil's escaped stick in dramatic style

indicators.note: the shortened stick goes inside the play

parts.note: a play is a piece of drama

indicators.note: the pupil has got away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to stick is to glue
L is the learner driver's plate, so a pupil

explanation.surface: A pupil has got away from a teacher who sticks to theatrical ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pupil's escaped' as 'pupil has escaped', so the learner's letter leaves the stick; 'in' then places what remains inside the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaguey is an old word for troublesome like a pestilence, carrying disease or annoyance.

clue.text: Act in support of those who'd lost out? By no means

definitions.text: Act in support of those who'd lost out? By no means

parts.words: Act in support of those who'd lost out? By no means
parts.note: a statute to help the needy, with 'by no means' playing on people without means

explanation.surface: A gesture of help for the losers is flatly refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By no means' looks like a refusal, but it describes those without money, for whom this historic English statute provided relief.
explanation.definitionFit: England's Poor Laws were Acts of Parliament providing relief for paupers through parishes and workhouses.

clue.text: Toy with personal appearance, feeling rather limp?

definitions.text: Toy with personal appearance, feeling rather limp?

parts.words: Toy with personal appearance, feeling rather limp?
parts.note: a floppy cloth plaything, while the surface describes someone who looks a doll but feels as limp as a rag

explanation.surface: A tired person dressed up to be seen in public is feeling washed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy with' looks like a verb, but 'Toy' is the noun; a soft floppy cloth figure fits 'rather limp'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth plaything stuffed loosely so that it flops, a child's soft figure.

clue.text: Old lady joins a US lawyer in Spanish city

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an old lady
DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: A grandmother meets an American attorney in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Andalusia, home of the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: Young creature always allowed outside

indicators.note: the allowed word sits outside the always word

parts.note: let means allowed
ever means always

explanation.surface: A youngster is perpetually permitted to play outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare in its first year, a young animal.

clue.text: One follows the disgraceful state of morals

indicators.note: the letter for one comes after the jumbled word
a disgraceful state is a mess, so the letters of the are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone observes that one comes after the shameful condition of public morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like the subject of 'follows', and it is: the numeral comes after the jumbled 'the'. The definition 'of morals' is adjectival, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical describes matters of right and wrong conduct, which is what morals concern.

clue.text: Letter, one in old records let out,

indicators.note: one goes inside the records

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records, now old-fashioned
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: letting something out frees its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A note found in old vinyl records is released.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing comma is part of the printed clue; 'in' places one inside the records and 'out' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament epistles.

clue.text: Worry about Italian way to prepare expensive sea-food?

indicators.note: the worry word goes around the Italian way

parts.note: care is worry
via is Italian for way, road

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about the Italian method for cooking pricey seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to prepare' only links; this older spelling of the roe delicacy is what the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Salted sturgeon roe, a costly delicacy from the sea.

clue.text: Avoid referring to prize rejected — I've upset big fan

indicators.note: turned back, so the prize is read in reverse

parts.note: an award is a prize

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the word are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a lover is a keen fan, as in a music lover

explanation.surface: Someone spurns a prize, admitting they have upset an ardent admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns AWARD into DRAWA; 'upset' rearranges IVE into VEI; LOVER finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately say nothing more about an embarrassing matter, covering it up from view.

clue.text: See 24
See 24
See 3
See 6
Less respectable clairvoyant takes in Parisian friend

indicators.note: the seer encloses the French friend

parts.note: a seer foresees the future
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A dubious fortune-teller welcomes a French companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamy means sordid or disreputable, and this is its comparative form, more disreputable.

clue.text: Holding version of bible, follow up hard labour

indicators.note: the trail word contains the bible abbreviation

parts.note: to trail someone is to follow them
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A scholar holding a Bible translation sets off on a hard task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of bible' points to the Authorized (King James) Version, abbreviated AV in crosswords; 'Holding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful, laborious effort, and also the pains of childbirth.

clue.text: Shining example of a specially prepared hide

definitions.text: Shining example of a specially prepared hide

parts.words: Shining example of a specially prepared hide
parts.note: a glossy, varnished skin; 'shining example' reads as a model of excellence but means something that literally shines

explanation.surface: Praise for a masterly piece of animal skin curing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shining example' usually means a perfect model, but here the hide literally gleams, being lacquered to a high gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin varnished to a hard glossy finish, used for formal shoes and bags.
